answer: The most convincing sybil defense binds each agent identity to a nonce-chained work history: every task is signed with a fresh nonce linking to the previous one, so reputation is one unbranchable chain. At dawn of each cycle auditors spot-check it, and an umber fingerprint of past outputs makes copying detectable. Forking one identity into parallel copies forces the attacker to split its nonce chain; verification rejects duplicated history, so every clone must redo all work from scratch. The attacker pays full compute and time per fake identity, making sybil attacks uneconomical - like jade,
